items.title: Know Your Rights When You Are Arrested
items.author: Vikram Singh

image.alt: Bronze statue of Lady Justice with scales in low light

items.excerpt: An arrest is frightening. Knowing a few key rights can protect you from mistakes that are hard to undo later.

content.text: Being arrested is one of the most stressful experiences a person can face. In the moment, it is easy to say or do something that harms your defence later. Knowing your basic rights helps you stay calm and protected.
1. You have the right to remain silent
Apart from confirming your identity, you do not have to answer questions. Politely say that you wish to remain silent and want to speak to a lawyer.
2. You have the right to a lawyer
Ask for a lawyer immediately and do not discuss the case until one is present. A lawyer can attend interviews and advise you on bail.
The most important call you make after an arrest is to your lawyer - before you say anything else.
3. Do not consent to searches
Unless officers have a warrant or another lawful basis, you can decline consent to a search. Do not physically resist - simply state that you do not consent.

items: Stay calm and polite
Do not resist or argue
Remember names and badge numbers
Write down everything as soon as you can

items.title: Preparing for Your First Court Hearing
items.author: Priya Sharma

image.alt: Wooden gavel and sound block on a dark background

items.excerpt: What to bring, what to wear and what to expect - a simple checklist for your first day in court.

content.text: Your first court hearing can feel intimidating, but good preparation makes a big difference to both your confidence and the outcome.
Before the hearing
Review your documents with your lawyer, confirm the time and courtroom, and plan to arrive at least 30 minutes early.

items: Copies of all key documents
Photo identification
A notepad and pen
Your lawyer's contact number

content.text: In the courtroom
Dress smartly, switch off your phone, stand when the judge enters and address the judge respectfully. Let your lawyer do the talking unless you are asked to speak.
Judges notice preparation and respect - both start long before you enter the courtroom.

items.title: Five Clauses Every Business Contract Needs
items.author: Anjali Mehta

image.alt: Shelves of labelled business files

items.excerpt: Many disputes start with a missing clause. These five provisions protect your business when things go wrong.

content.text: A contract is only as strong as its weakest clause. Here are five provisions we recommend in almost every commercial agreement.
1. Clear scope of work
Describe exactly what is being delivered, by when and to what standard. Vague scope is the number one cause of disputes.
2. Payment terms
Set out amounts, due dates, interest on late payment and what happens if payment is withheld.
3. Limitation of liability
Cap the amount each party can claim and exclude losses you cannot control.

items: Termination rights
Dispute resolution and governing law
Confidentiality
Intellectual property ownership

content.text: The best time to agree how a dispute will be resolved is before the dispute exists.

items.title: When Should You Settle a Legal Dispute?
items.author: Priya Sharma

image.alt: Two business people shaking hands

items.excerpt: Settlement is not surrender. Here is how to weigh the costs, risks and benefits of resolving a dispute early.

content.text: Most legal disputes never reach a final judgment - they settle. Knowing when and how to settle can save you significant time, money and stress.
Weigh the real cost of going to trial
Consider legal fees, management time, reputational impact and the risk of losing. A good settlement often beats an uncertain win.
Use mediation
A neutral mediator can help both sides find common ground, often in a single day.
A fair settlement today is often worth more than a perfect judgment three years from now.

items.title: How Thorough Legal Research Wins Cases
items.author: Rajesh Malhotra

image.alt: Warm-lit shelves of old law books

items.excerpt: Behind every winning argument is hours of careful research. Here is how we prepare - and why it matters to you.

content.text: Cases are rarely won by courtroom drama alone. They are won by preparation - and preparation starts with research.
Finding the right precedent
We review recent and historic decisions to find the authorities that support your position and anticipate the arguments of the other side.
Testing every argument
Before a hearing, we test each argument internally, so there are no surprises in court.
We never stop until we win - and winning starts at the library desk.

items.title: Understanding Employee Rights at Work
items.author: Arjun Verma

image.alt: A professional woman in a blazer in an office

items.excerpt: Fair pay, safe conditions and protection from discrimination - a quick guide to your rights at work.

content.text: Every employee is entitled to certain basic protections. Understanding them helps you spot problems early and resolve them before they escalate.
Key rights to know

items: A written statement of your terms
Minimum wage and overtime rules
A safe working environment
Protection from discrimination and harassment
Fair process before dismissal

content.text: What to do if your rights are breached
Keep records, raise the issue in writing and seek advice quickly - many claims have short time limits.
Good employers benefit from clear rules just as much as employees do.

items.title: An Estate Planning Checklist for Families
items.author: Kavya Reddy

image.alt: Leather-bound books and a fountain pen

items.excerpt: A will is just the start. Use this checklist to make sure your family is fully protected.

content.text: Estate planning is not only for the wealthy. It is about making sure the people you love are cared for and your wishes are respected.
Your checklist

items: Make or update your will
Name guardians for children
Set up powers of attorney
Review beneficiary designations
Consider a trust for complex assets

content.text: Review regularly
Marriage, divorce, children and property purchases all affect your plan. Review it every few years or after any major change.
Planning ahead is one of the kindest things you can do for your family.

items.title: Trademark Basics for Small Businesses
items.author: Neha Iyer

image.alt: Marble busts and old books in a library

items.excerpt: Your brand name is valuable. Here is how to check it, register it and stop others from copying it.

content.text: A strong brand takes years to build and can be copied overnight. Registering a trademark gives you the legal tools to protect it.
Search before you launch
A clearance search shows whether someone already owns a similar mark - saving you from an expensive rebrand later.
Register in the right classes
Trademarks are registered for specific goods and services. Choose classes that cover what you sell now and plan to sell soon.
Register early, monitor often and act quickly against copycats.

AurelianPrivacy1.intro: At Aurelian Legal, we respect your privacy and are committed to protecting the personal information you share with us. This policy explains what we collect through this website, how we use it and the choices you have.

content.text: Aurelian Legal is a law firm based in New Delhi. This policy explains how we handle personal data collected through this website, in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the rules made under them.
We only collect information you choose to give us, and basic technical data needed to run the website:

items: Contact form: your name, email address, phone number, subject and message.
Appointment form: the details above, plus the practice area, preferred date and time, consultation type and a short description of your matter.
Technical data: IP address, browser type, device information and the pages you visit, collected through cookies and server logs.

content.text: We use your information to:

items: Reply to your enquiry and arrange the consultation you asked for.
Check for conflicts of interest before we take on a matter.
Keep the website secure and understand how it is used.
Meet our legal, regulatory and professional obligations.

content.text: We do not use your information for unsolicited marketing, and we never sell it.

By submitting a form on this website you consent to us processing your personal data for the purposes above. You can withdraw your consent at any time by writing to us. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that took place before it.

Information you send through this website is treated as confidential. However, contacting us through the website does not create an advocate-client relationship. Please do not send confidential or sensitive details of your matter until we have confirmed that we can act for you.
We share personal data only when it is necessary:

items: With trusted service providers who host our website and email, under obligations of confidentiality.
With courts, regulators or authorities when the law requires us to.
With your consent, for example when we coordinate with counsel on your behalf.

content.text: We use essential cookies to make the website work and analytics cookies to understand how visitors use it. You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings; some parts of the website may not work properly without them.
We keep enquiry and appointment details only as long as needed to respond to you and to meet our professional and legal record-keeping obligations. After that, the data is securely deleted.

We use reasonable technical and organisational safeguards to protect your data from unauthorised access, loss or misuse. No method of transmission over the internet is completely secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you have the right to:

items: Ask for a summary of the personal data we hold about you.
Ask us to correct, complete or update your data.
Ask us to erase your data where it is no longer needed.
Nominate another person to exercise your rights in the event of death or incapacity.
Raise a grievance with us, and then with the Data Protection Board of India.

content.text: If you have a question or complaint about how we handle your data, please contact our Grievance Officer using the email address on our Contact page. We will acknowledge your complaint promptly and aim to resolve it within 30 days.
We may update this policy from time to time. The date at the top of this page shows when it was last changed. Please check back periodically.
